channel.title: rahul.london
channel.description: Writing, systems, and notes by Rahul Goma Phulore.

item.title: Composable table updates in Slick
item.description: Using existential types to build composable, type-safe update operations in Slick.

item.title: Types of map function in Haskell, Scala, and Clojure
item.description: A comparative look at how Haskell, Scala, and Clojure generalise `map` in different directions.

item.title: Dead-simple threading with functions, in Clojure
item.description: A small function-based alternative to Clojure's threading macros, built from composable combinators instead of syntax transformation.

item.title: So how much of inheritance criticism is really valid?
item.description: A look at whether the fragile-base-class problem is really specific to inheritance, or whether selective overriding is the deeper issue.

item.title: Understanding monads
item.description: A transcript-style introduction to monads through Scala examples involving optional values, exceptions, and futures.

item.title: Not-so-embedded documents with Clojure
item.description: Using metadata and multimethods in Clojure to get polymorphic behaviour over plain maps without wrapping them in classes.

item.title: Easing the use of the Embedded Document pattern
item.description: Using small Ruby combinators to reduce boilerplate when wrapping JSON with the Embedded Document pattern.

item.title: Something to be said for dynamic typing
item.description: A short note pointing to Rahul's Quora answer on what dynamic typing can make possible, especially in contrast with Scala.

item.title: Stacking up Factor against the Lisp bullet list
item.description: Notes from revisiting Factor, prompted by a Twitter exchange about how its macro system and broader design compare with Lisp.

item.title: F# Option Cheat Sheet
item.description: A compact guide to working with F# options through higher-order functions instead of repetitive pattern matching.

item.title: Sections of (.)
item.description: A small note on learning to read Haskell expressions that use sections of `(.)`, and the explanation that finally made them click.

item.title: 10 Factor One-Liners to Impress Your Friends
item.description: A first pass at the classic “one-liners to impress your friends” meme, translated into Factor after discovering the language through Slava Pestov’s talk.

item.title: Emulating C#’s default keyword in Scala, and putting it on steroids
item.description: Using Scala’s type system to emulate C#’s default keyword and then extend it with typeclass-driven defaults.
